answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a relic, before it can post or attest. Forging 273 aliases as a result costs 332 bonds held for 3 days each, plus the anchor attestations those aliases can never earn. A single harbor checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
